Memory as Fluid Mechanics

Memory processes mapped directly onto fluid mechanics concepts (reservoirs, vortices, laminar/turbulent zones, boundary layers, pressure gradients/waves)

How the Mapping Works

  • Reservoir (Long-term Memory) — Stores accumulated traces; modeled in population dynamics (e.g., Wilson–Cowan) as stable attractors (Cowan, 2016; Chow & Karimipanah, 2020).
  • Channel (Working Memory) — Information flow can be laminar (maintenance) or become turbulent (interference/recombination). Whole-brain analyses report turbulence-like dynamics aiding fast information transfer (Deco et al., 2020; 2023).
  • Pressure Gradient (Attention) — Salience and goals create energy differentials that route content into the channel (conceptual link to control of neural gain).
  • Boundary Layer (Event Boundaries) — Perceptual boundaries act like shear layers that reorganize encoding and forgetting rates (Logie et al., 2021; Jafarpour et al., 2022).
  • Replay & Reverberation — Traveling/standing waves during rest/sleep support consolidation and planning (Chen et al., 2023; Huelin Gorriz et al., 2023).
  • Diffusion on Networks — Spreading activation/random walks over semantic networks approximate search/retrieval (Vitevitch et al., 2021; Kumar et al., 2022).
